title: The dsc command line
preamble:
# The dsc command line

The `dsc` command-line surface: the subcommands, what
each produces, the exit codes, and the flags whose effect on the artefact a
grammar cannot carry.

**The shape of the command line is a grammar and lives in a file.**
`compiler/dsc_cli.ebnf` is the normative statement of what invocations are
admissible ([STYL.2.15.6.2]); this document is the residue ([STYL.2.15.4]) —
what the admissible invocations *do*, which no production can say.

**This is the product, not one implementation of it.** Any conforming compiler
owes this surface, so it sits in `runtime/` beside the clauses describing
the artefact a compile produces, on the same split `[STYL.2.13.6]` draws for
ahead-of-time compilation: the product commitment here, each implementation's
account of meeting it in `impl/`.

Prefix `RCLI`.

Paired with:
- `compiler/dsc_cli.ebnf` — the invocation grammar this document is the
  residue of.
- [RDSC] — the artefact `compile` produces.
- [RLOW] — the Rete network it carries.

## What this is not

- Not an account of any compiler's internals. How a subcommand is dispatched,
  and what modules implement it, is `impl/` material ([STYL.2.13.5]).
- Not the invocation grammar. That is `compiler/dsc_cli.ebnf`, and restating a
  production here would be the duplication [STYL.2.15.1] refuses.
